claims.text: Cast refractory multi-principal-element alloys can exhibit limited ambient-temperature ductility.
HfMoTaTiZr can have a single-phase BCC constitution in its reference state.
Aging refractory high-entropy alloys can produce silicide, B2, or Laves secondary phases.
Multistage thermomechanical processing can create stepwise, independently controllable coherent nanoprecipitation in a supersaturated W-based matrix.
The coherent precipitates produced by the cited W-based process can include D0a Ni3Ta-based delta precipitates and D022 gamma-double-prime precipitates.
High-pressure torsion or equal-channel angular pressing followed by aging will refine the proposed refractory alloy to grains below 50 nm.
Processing temperature and strain rate can be tuned to retain a supersaturated matrix while selectively nucleating coherent precipitates.
A processing window exists that nucleates D0a or D022 precipitates while avoiding the stability windows of Laves, B2, silicide, and other TCP phases.
A high density of coherent precipitate-matrix interfaces will stabilize a grain size below 50 nm.
Coherent nanoprecipitates act as barriers to dislocation motion and provide precipitation strengthening.
Fine grains and precipitation can jointly provide grain-boundary strengthening and precipitation strengthening in refractory multi-principal-element alloys.
Precipitation hardening can produce significant strengthening and progressive multistage strain hardening in refractory high-entropy alloys.
Intrinsically brittle silicide, B2, and Laves secondary phases can limit ambient-temperature tensile behavior in refractory high-entropy alloys.
The proposed process will produce a nanocrystalline BCC matrix containing coherent nanoprecipitates as a dual-phase structure.
The processed alloy will have ambient-temperature yield strength above 2000 MPa and uniform tensile ductility above 10%.
The processed microstructure will contain no detectable Laves or silicide phases.
Conventional cast HfMoTaTiZr typically develops Laves or B2 phases and has fracture strain below 5%.
Aging above the coherent-precipitate solvus will cause coarsening or transformation into incoherent brittle Laves or silicide phases.
An insufficient processing strain rate will prevent refinement below 50 nm.
Aging at 800-1000 degrees Celsius is known to induce Laves-phase formation in systems sufficiently similar to the proposed HfMoTaTiZr experiment.

contradictions.description: The target is called a dual-phase solid-solution structure, but the proposed second phases are ordered D0a or D022 precipitates rather than a second solid-solution phase.

The prediction requires uniform tensile ductility above 10%, whereas the falsification rule uses fracture strain above 5% and does not falsify all outcomes that miss the claimed ductility. For example, a strong but very brittle sample without detected intermetallics could evade the stated rule.
